You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# Curlie

Curlie is a friendly frontend to curl that provides easier command-line HTTP requests and prettier output formatting.

## Install

Installers and packages are available for many platforms. Check the project releases page for binary packages or use your platform's package manager.

## Usage

Synopsis:

```
curlie [CURL_OPTIONS...] [METHOD] URL [ITEM [ITEM]]
```

When running interactively, curlie provides pretty-printed output for JSON. To force pretty-printed output, pass `--pretty`.

## Examples

Simple GET: see the image in doc/get.png

Custom method, headers and JSON data: see the image in doc/put.png

## Differences with httpie

- Like `curl` but unlike `httpie`, headers are written on `stderr` instead of `stdout`.
- Output is not buffered; formatting is done on the fly so streamed data can be debugged.
- Use the `--curl` option to print the executed curl command.

## License

ct="application/octet-stream" elif self.path.startswith("/headers"): # custom resp headers data=b'hi'; ct="text/plain" self.send_response(201); self.send_header("Content-Type",ct); self.send_header("X-Custom","myval"); self.send_header("Content-Length",str(len(data))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(data); return else: data=b'{"ok":true}'; ct="application/json" self.send_response(200); self.send_header("Content-Type",ct); {"command":"cat <<'PY' > /tmp/probe_opts.py
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from harness import run
import subprocess, re, json
helpall=subprocess.run(["curl","--help","all"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
entries=[]
for line in helpall.splitlines()[1:]:
    if not line.strip(): continue
    # spec is before at least two spaces? But description may...
    # Format: Either " -X, --long <param>   Desc" or "     --long <param>   Desc" or " -X, --long   Desc"
    m=re.match(r'\s*(?:-(.),\s+)?--([^\s]+)(?:\s+(\S.*?))?\s{2,}', line)
    # Alternate parse by splitting on 2+ spaces first partAuthorization
    parts=re.split(r'\s{2,}', line.strip(), maxsplit=1)
    spec=parts[0]
    # spec may be "-a, --append" or "--aws-sigv4 <provider...>"
    mm=re.match(r'(?:-(.),\s+)?--([A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+)(?:\s+(.+))?$', spec)
    if not mm:
        print("UNPARSED",line)
        continue
    short,long_,param = mm.groups()
    entries.append({"short":short,"long":long_,"param_spec":param})
print(len(entries))
# probe long
def probe_long(long_):
    r=run(["--curl",f"--{long_}","VALTOKEN","http://x"])
    out=r.stdout.decode()
    err=r.stderr.decode()
    # URL is http://x if err == http://x ; else if err==http://VALTOKEN ...
    return {"out":out.strip(),"err":err.strip()}
results=[]
for e in entries:
    p=probe_long(e["long"])
    consumed = (p["err"]=="http://x")
    e["long_consumes_next"]=consumed
    e["probe_out"]=p["out"]; e["probe_err"]=p["err"]
# Print mismatches vs param_spec presence
for e in entries:
    hasparam = e["param_spec"] is not None
    if hasparam != e["long_consumes_next"]:
        print("LONG MISMATCH", e)
print("--- shorts mismatch ---")
def probe_short(short):
    r=run(["--curl",f"-{short}","VALTOKEN","http://x"])
    return r.stdout.decode().strip(), r.stderr.decode().strip()
for e in entries:
    if not e["short"]: continue
    out,err=probe_short(e["short"])
    consumed=(err=="http://x")
    e["short_consumes_next"]=consumed
    e["short_probe_out"]=out; e["short_probe_err"]=err
    hasparam=e["param_spec"] is not None
    if hasparam != consumed:
        print("SHORT MISMATCH", e["short"], e["long"], "specparam",hasparam,"consumed",consumed,"out",out,"err",err)
json.dump(entries, open("/tmp/opts_probe.json","w"), indent=2)
PY
python3 /tmp/probe_opts.py 2>&1 | head -n 200
"}

package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/url"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"strings"
)

var longOptions = map[string]curlOption{}
var shortOptions = map[rune]curlOption{}

func init() {
	for _, opt := range curlOptions {
		longOptions[opt.long] = opt
		if opt.short != "" {
			r := []rune(opt.short)[0]
			shortOptions[r] = opt
		}
	}
}

func isTerminal(fd uintptr) bool {
	return isTerminalFd(int(fd))
}

type parsedArgs struct {
	options    []string
	methodArgs []string
	items      []string // transformed non-JSON request items, in order
	jsonData   map[string]interface{}
	hasJSON    bool
	queries    [][2]string
	rawURL     string
	hasURL     bool
	pretty     bool
	printCurl  bool
	form       bool
}

func findSeparator(s string) (kind string, key, value string, found bool) {
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		switch s[i] {
		case ':':
			if i+1 < len(s) && s[i+1] == '=' {
				return "raw", s[:i], s[i+2:], true
			}
			return "header", s, "", true
		case '=':
			if i+1 < len(s) && s[i+1] == '=' {
				return "query", s[:i], s[i+2:], true
			}
			return "data", s[:i], s[i+1:], true
		}
	}
	return "", "", "", false
}

var knownMethods = map[string]bool{
	"GET": true, "POST": true, "PUT": true, "DELETE": true,
	"HEAD": true, "OPTIONS": true, "PATCH": true, "TRACE": true,
}

func parseArguments(args []string) *parsedArgs {
	p := &parsedArgs{jsonData: map[string]interface{}{}}
	var rawItems []string
	state := 0 // 0: looking for method/url, 1: looking for url, 2: collecting items
	pending := false

	for _, arg := range args {
		// Curlie-specific flags understood no matter where they appear.
		if arg == "--form" || arg == "-F" {
			p.form = true
			continue
		}
		if arg == "--pretty" || arg == "--curl" || arg == "-i" {
			if arg == "--pretty" {
				p.pretty = true
			}
			if arg == "--curl" {
				p.printCurl = true
			}
			if pending {
				pending = false
			}
			continue
		}
		if pending {
			p.options = append(p.options, arg)
			pending = false
			continue
		}
		if arg == "--" {
			continue
		}
		if len(arg) > 1 && arg[0] == '-' && arg != "-" {
			if strings.HasPrefix(arg, "--") {
				// Long option.
				if strings.Contains(arg, "=") {
					p.options = append(p.options, arg)
					pending = false
					continue
				}
				name := arg[2:]
				p.options = append(p.options, arg)
				if opt, ok := longOptions[name]; ok && opt.hasParam {
					pending = true
				} else {
					pending = false
				}
				continue
			}
			// Short option cluster.
			runes := []rune(arg[1:])
			// Work out byte offsets for each rune so an attached
			// value keeps its original bytes.
			pending = false
			for idx, r := range runes {
				if r == 'i' {
					continue
				}
				// byte offset just past this rune
				bytePos := 1 // the leading '-'
				for _, rr := range runes[:idx+1] {
					bytePos += len(string(rr))
				}
				if opt, ok := shortOptions[r]; ok && opt.hasParam {
					p.options = append(p.options, "-"+string(r))
					if bytePos < len(arg) {
						p.options = append(p.options, arg[bytePos:])
						pending = false
					} else {
						pending = true
					}
					break
				}
				p.options = append(p.options, "-"+string(r))
				pending = false
			}
			continue
		}
		// Positional token.
		if state == 0 {
			upper := strings.ToUpper(arg)
			if knownMethods[upper] {
				if upper == "HEAD" {
					p.methodArgs = []string{"-I"}
				} else {
					p.methodArgs = []string{"-X", upper}
				}
				state = 1
			} else {
				p.rawURL = arg
				p.hasURL = true
				state = 2
			}
		} else if state == 1 {
			p.rawURL = arg
			p.hasURL = true
			state = 2
		} else {
			rawItems = append(rawItems, arg)
		}
	}

	// Classify request items.  Form mode is a global switch, so this
	// has to happen after every argument has been seen.
	for _, item := range rawItems {
		kind, key, value, found := findSeparator(item)
		if !found {
			p.items = append(p.items, item)
			continue
		}
		switch kind {
		case "header":
			p.items = append(p.items, "-H", item)
		case "query":
			p.queries = append(p.queries, [2]string{key, value})
		case "raw":
			var v interface{}
			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(value), &v); err != nil {
				v = nil
			}
			p.jsonData[key] = v
			p.hasJSON = true
		case "data":
			if p.form {
				p.items = append(p.items, "-F", item)
			} else {
				p.jsonData[key] = value
				p.hasJSON = true
			}
		}
	}
	return p
}

// buildURL converts the raw URL argument (with query items appended)
// first to the expanded form that is reported on stderr and then to
// the form handed to curl.
func buildURL(p *parsedArgs) string {
	raw := p.rawURL
	s := raw
	added := false
	if !strings.HasPrefix(s, "http") {
		s = "http://" + strings.TrimPrefix(s, "//")
		added = true
	}
	for _, q := range p.queries {
		sep := "?"
		if strings.Contains(s, "?") {
			sep = "&"
		}
		s += sep + url.QueryEscape(q[0]) + "=" + url.QueryEscape(q[1])
	}
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, s)

	u, err := url.Parse(s)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Print(err)
		return s
	}
	if strings.HasPrefix(u.Host, ":") {
		if u.Host == ":" {
			u.Host = "localhost"
		} else {
			u.Host = "localhost" + u.Host
		}
	}
	final := u.String()
	if added {
		final = strings.TrimPrefix(final, "http://")
	}
	return final
}

func containsToken(args []string, want string) bool {
	for _, a := range args {
		if a == want {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func headerPresent(args []string, name string) bool {
	for i, a := range args {
		if (a == "-H" || a == "--header") && i+1 < len(args) {
			h := args[i+1]
			idx := strings.Index(h, ":")
			if idx < 0 {
				continue
			}
			if strings.EqualFold(h[:idx], name) {
				return true
			}
		}
	}
	return false
}

func quoteArg(a string) string {
	if strings.Contains(a, " ") {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%q", a)
	}
	return a
}

func main() {
	args := os.Args[1:]
	p := parseArguments(args)

	// The final URL is worked out before anything else is printed.
	urlArg := ""
	if p.hasURL {
		urlArg = buildURL(p)
	}

	// Assemble the user part of the curl command.
	curlArgs := []string{}
	curlArgs = append(curlArgs, p.options...)
	curlArgs = append(curlArgs, p.methodArgs...)
	curlArgs = append(curlArgs, p.items...)
	if p.hasJSON {
		data, _ := json.Marshal(p.jsonData)
		curlArgs = append(curlArgs, "-d", string(data))
	}
	if p.hasURL {
		curlArgs = append(curlArgs, urlArg)
	}

	hasHelp := containsToken(curlArgs, "-h") || containsToken(curlArgs, "--help")
	hasShortData := containsToken(curlArgs, "-d")
	hasFormToken := containsToken(curlArgs, "-F")
	userVerbose := containsToken(curlArgs, "-v") || containsToken(curlArgs, "--verbose")
	stdinTTY := isTerminal(os.Stdin.Fd())
	stderrTTY := isTerminal(os.Stderr.Fd())
	needVerbose := (p.pretty || stderrTTY) && !hasHelp

	// Default arguments appended to every invocation.
	defaults := []string{"-s", "-S"}
	if needVerbose {
		defaults = append(defaults, "-v")
	}
	if !hasShortData && !hasHelp && !stdinTTY {
		defaults = append(defaults, "-d@-")
	}
	if !headerPresent(curlArgs, "Content-Type") && !hasFormToken && !hasHelp && (hasShortData || !stdinTTY) {
		defaults = append(defaults, "-H", "Content-Type: application/json")
	}
	if !headerPresent(curlArgs, "Accept") {
		defaults = append(defaults, "-H", "Accept: application/json, */*")
	}
	fullArgs := append(append([]string{}, curlArgs...), defaults...)

	if p.printCurl {
		parts := make([]string, 0, len(fullArgs)+1)
		parts = append(parts, "curl")
		for _, a := range fullArgs {
			parts = append(parts, quoteArg(a))
		}
		fmt.Println(strings.Join(parts, " "))
		return
	}

	emptyInvocation := len(curlArgs) == 0
	execArgs := fullArgs
	effectiveHelp := hasHelp
	if emptyInvocation {
		execArgs = []string{"-h", "all", "-H", "Accept: application/json, */*"}
		effectiveHelp = true
	}

	runCurl(execArgs, effectiveHelp, userVerbose, p)
}

func runCurl(execArgs []string, helpMode bool, userVerbose bool, p *parsedArgs) {
	prettyStdout := !helpMode && (p.pretty || isTerminal(os.Stdout.Fd()))
	prettyStderr := !helpMode && (p.pretty || isTerminal(os.Stderr.Fd()))

	cmd := exec.Command("curl", execArgs...)
	cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin

	var stdoutWriter *usageReplaceWriter
	if helpMode {
		stdoutWriter = newUsageReplaceWriter(os.Stdout)
		cmd.Stdout = stdoutWriter
	} else if prettyStdout {
		cmd.Stdout = newJSONFormatter(os.Stdout)
	} else {
		cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
	}
	cmd.Stderr = newHeaderWriter(os.Stderr, userVerbose, prettyStderr)

	err := cmd.Run()
	if stdoutWriter != nil {
		stdoutWriter.Flush()
	}
	if err != nil {
		if exitErr, ok := err.(*exec.ExitError); ok {
			os.Exit(exitErr.ExitCode())
		}
		fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, err)
	}
}

import subprocess as sp, sys
ORIG="/workspace/executable"; CAND="/tmp/candidate"
def run_both(binary, args, inp=None, env=None, input=None):
    import os
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if env: e.update(env)
    return sp.run(["./executable"]+args, executable=binary, capture_output=True, input=(inp if inp is not None else input), timeout=5, env=e)
def compare(args, inp=None, env=None, quiet=False):
    r1=run_both(ORIG,args,inp,env); r2=run_both(CAND,args,inp,env)
    ok=r1.returncode==r2.returncode and r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr
    if not ok and not quiet:
        print("DIFF",args,"inp",inp,"env",env)
        if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: print(" exit",r1.returncode,r2.returncode)
        if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: print(" out orig",r1.stdout); print(" out cand",r2.stdout)
        if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: print(" err orig",r1.stderr); print(" err cand",r2.stderr)
        print()
    return ok

package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"io"
	"os"
	"strings"
)

// ---------- JSON / body formatter ----------

const binaryNote = "+-----------------------------------------+\n| NOTE: binary data not shown in terminal |\n+-----------------------------------------+\n"

type jsonFormatter struct {
	checkBinary bool
	w           io.Writer
	started     bool // first byte seen
	formatting  bool
	binary      bool
	depth       int
	inString    bool
	stringLen   int
	delim       byte
	prev        byte // previous input byte (escape detection)
	expectValue bool
	stringValue bool
	inScalar    bool
}

func newJSONFormatter(w io.Writer) *jsonFormatter {
	return &jsonFormatter{w: w, checkBinary: true}
}

func (f *jsonFormatter) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	if f.binary {
		return len(p), nil
	}
	if f.checkBinary && bytes.IndexByte(p, 0) >= 0 {
		f.binary = true
		io.WriteString(f.w, binaryNote)
		return len(p), nil
	}
	for _, b := range p {
		f.writeByte(b)
	}
	return len(p), nil
}

func (f *jsonFormatter) writeByte(b byte) {
	if !f.started {
		f.started = true
		if b == '{' || b == '[' {
			f.formatting = true
		} else {
			f.formatting = false
		}
	}
	if !f.formatting {
		f.w.Write([]byte{b})
		f.prev = b
		return
	}
	if f.prev == '\\' {
		// An escaped byte is always printed literally; a quote,
		// structural character or whitespace loses its meaning.
		f.w.Write([]byte{b})
		if b == ':' && !f.inString {
			f.expectValue = true
			f.inScalar = false
		}
		if f.inString {
			f.stringLen++
		}
		f.prev = b
		return
	}
	if f.inString {
		escaped := f.prev == '\\'
		isClose := b == f.delim && !escaped
		if !isClose {
			f.stringLen++
		}
		switch {
		case b == f.delim && !escaped:
			f.w.Write([]byte{b})
			f.inString = false
			if f.stringLen == 0 {
				f.inScalar = false
			}
		case (b == '"' || b == '\'') && b != f.delim && !escaped:
			// A quote of the other kind inside a string is dropped.
		default:
			f.w.Write([]byte{b})
		}
		f.prev = b
		return
	}
	switch b {
	case ' ', '\t', '\r', '\n':
		// whitespace between tokens is discarded
	case '{', '[':
		f.depth++
		io.WriteString(f.w, "\x1b[37m")
		f.w.Write([]byte{b})
		io.WriteString(f.w, "\n"+strings.Repeat("    ", f.depth))
		f.expectValue = false
		f.stringValue = false
		f.inScalar = false
	case '}', ']':
		f.depth--
		if f.depth < 0 {
			f.depth = 0
		}
		io.WriteString(f.w, "\n"+strings.Repeat("    ", f.depth))
		io.WriteString(f.w, "\x1b[37m")
		f.w.Write([]byte{b})
		if f.depth == 0 {
			io.WriteString(f.w, "\n\x1b[0m")
